#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pre-push — the live-spec push gate (SPEC M-6; scope grown by prover findings F7/F4;
# gate e added for INV-17, the prototype fence).
# Blocks a push unless every gate below passes.
#
# Generic pattern for a host project: copy this file, then in guardrails/README.md's
# "how a host adapts" section swap in your own test command and prover cadence — the
# gate shape (fresh review record / green tests / ownership / coverage) travels as-is.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"
GUARDRAILS="$REPO_ROOT/guardrails"

# -- deletion-only stand-down (SPEC INV-290, ROADMAP row 502) --
# git feeds this hook one ref-update line per pushed ref on stdin (githooks(5)); read it ONCE, here,
# before any gate below can touch stdin — a manual invocation for testing leaves stdin as a tty and
# must never block on a read. A push whose every fed line deletes its remote counterpart (the
# all-zero local object id) carries no content for any gate to judge, so the whole chain stands down
# by name instead of falling to the reach map's conservative FULL — the fix for the 2026-07-27 hang
# (four tag deletions read as an empty diff, fell to the full suite, died on the two-minute limit).
# This check carries no gate letter: it is a triage read ahead of the chain, the placement
# check-push-reach.sh already holds inside gate b, not a net that blocks on red.

# The marker below is the machine-readable half of the convention guardrails/check-prover-record.sh
# states in full: every arm that can let a push past the prover-record demand carries one
# `# STAND-DOWN: <name>` line, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must name that same <name>.
# tests/test_deletion_only_push.py reads both directions off these markers.
# STAND-DOWN: deletion-only
if [ -t 0 ]; then
  PUSH_REF_LINES=""
else
  PUSH_REF_LINES="$(cat)"
fi
export PUSH_REF_LINES
if [ -n "$PUSH_REF_LINES" ]; then
  set +e
  del_out="$("$GUARDRAILS/check-deletion-only-push.sh")"
  del_code=$?

## Findings

1. **False positive: `git clean -fn` / `-nf` is denied though it is a harmless no-op.** `hooks/worker-restore-guard.py`'s `matched_form()` (the `sub == "clean"` branch) flags any flag string containing `f` or `x`, so `-fn` and `-nf` both match `"git clean -f/-x"` and are denied. Verified against real git in a scratch repo: `git clean -fn` prints "Would remove …" and deletes nothing — git's own `-n`/`--dry-run` overrides `-f` when both are given. This is exactly the failure class the project's own docstrings call "the worse of the two failures" (a false refusal stops honest work) — quoted verbatim in `tests/test_worker_restore_guard.py`'s header — yet no case in the 41-case suite exercises `-fn`/`-nf`. The bug is inherited unchanged from `guardrails/check-worker-restore.py`'s `classify()` (same `"f" in a or "x" in a` test, untouched by this range), but 08ab1afd now makes it a live, blocking PreToolUse deny instead of a retrospective report.

2. **False negative: `git checkout -q .` is not denied, though it verifiably discards uncommitted work.** `matched_form()`'s checkout branch only checks `"--" in rest or rest[:1] == ["."]` — the token immediately following `checkout` must be the literal `.`. A leading flag defeats the match entirely. Verified against real git: `git checkout -q .` silently reverted a modified tracked file back to its last-committed content. This directly contradicts the hook's own docstring, which states: "A flag such as `-q` changes nothing about which of the five forms a command is, and this hook reads past it the same way `check-worker-restore.py`'s `classify()` does" — false for the bare-dot form (true only for the `-- <path>` form, which the test suite does cover via `test_checkout_dash_dash_quiet_denied`). `check-worker-restore.py`'s `classify()` has the identical gap, so the retrospective gate would also miss this exact command — both layers of the advertised two-layer defense have a real, trivially-typed hole.

3. **Related false negative: `git checkout HEAD file.txt` (or any treeish + path with no `--`) is not denied.** This is valid git syntax and, verified against real git, discards the named file's uncommitted changes just as `git checkout -- file.txt` does. Same root cause as #2 (the matcher only recognizes `--` or bare `.`, not a treeish followed by a pathspec).

4. **Unsupported/false claim in the code comment: the "drift test" it cites does not exist.** `hooks/worker-restore-guard.py` (lines ~76-79) states: "duplicated rather than imported... A drift test (`tests/test_worker_restore_guard.py`) runs both matchers over one shared table of commands so the two never silently diverge on what they catch." Verified: `tests/test_worker_restore_guard.py` never imports or references `guardrails/check-worker-restore.py` or its `classify()` — it only subprocess-runs the new hook against a fixed command table. `tests/test_worker_restore.py` (the pre-existing suite for `check-worker-restore.py`, untouched by this range) likewise never mentions the new hook. No mechanism actually guards the two duplicated matchers against silently diverging, contrary to the explicit claim — and findings #1-#3 show the two matchers currently agree only because they share the same bugs, not because anything checks that they agree.

5. **Internal numeric inconsistency in the docstring's own justification.** `hooks/worker-restore-guard.py` (lines 6-9) states "Twelve real occurrences... landed in one 24-hour window ending 2026-08-19 (`python3 guardrails/check-worker-restore.py --since-hours 24`: 15 ran, 1 declined...)" and later repeats "workers ran the command anyway, twelve times in a day." The citation given as support reports 15 "ran" (16 total records), not 12 — the headline number and its own cited evidence don't agree, in the same paragraph, undercutting the quantitative case built for shipping this gate as urgent.

## Blocking
1. `hooks/worker-restore-guard.py`'s clean-flag matcher denies the harmless `git clean -fn`/`-nf` dry-run (false positive — the class of failure this project explicitly treats as worse).
2. `hooks/worker-restore-guard.py`'s checkout matcher does not deny `git checkout -q .` (or any flag-before-dot form), which verifiably discards uncommitted work — a false negative that also contradicts the hook's own docstring claim about flags not mattering, and is unfixed in both the new hook and the pre-existing retrospective gate it duplicates.
3. Same matcher does not deny `git checkout <treeish> <path>` without `--` (e.g. `git checkout HEAD file.txt`), also verifiably discarding uncommitted work.
4. The docstring's claim of a "drift test" keeping the hook's matcher and `check-worker-restore.py`'s `classify()` from silently diverging is false — no such test exists anywhere in the repo.
5. The docstring's own headline incident count ("twelve") contradicts the number in its own cited command output ("15 ran, 1 declined").
